title: The anti-AI crowd didn't stop AI; they just forced it into the shadows.
author: ritsulover
selftext:
The world that anti-AI activists dream of isn't coming. If anything, their movement has only forced companies to get better at hiding the tracks.

A lot of anti-AI artists keep convincing themselves that GenAI is just "garbage tech" that will eventually implode, forcing corporations to crawl back and beg real artists for forgiveness. They love the idea of a massive consumer boycott the moment an AI fingerprint is detected, thinking the market will inevitably side with human creators.

But the reality is moving in the exact opposite direction.

GenAI is already being hard-wired into game development workflows. Industry surveys show 90% of game devs are already integrating some form of AI. Even here in Korea, giants like Nexon and Shift Up see AI as a mandatory evolution. Shift Up’s CEO, Kim Hyung-tae, has basically said that using AI is a survival requirement to stay competitive globally.

But here’s the kicker: whenever Shift Up faces backlash for suspected AI usage, their official stance is always, "We didn't use GenAI."

That is the core issue. It’s not that these companies are abandoning AI—they’ve just learned that the term "AI" is a PR nightmare that pisses off their customer base. In the art industry right now, if you’re strictly anti-AI, you’re just shrinking your own career prospects. From what I’ve seen on the ground, the question isn’t "Can you use AI?" anymore. It’s "How naturally can you bake it into your workflow?"

Most studios I know are already using their own fine-tuned LoRAs and internal AI pipelines. It’s not just about efficiency—it’s an insurance policy against "leaks." Using an off-the-shelf model is a liability, but if you call it "proprietary data" or an "artist-assisted tool," the legal and ethical gray area becomes much easier to navigate.

We’re already seeing major titles clearly using AI, yet the response is always the same:

"We didn't use it."

"The artist did it manually."

"Trust us."

And honestly? The public has no way to prove otherwise. You can’t verify the data, the model, or the extent of the usage from the outside. Eventually, the company says "no," the controversy dies down, and people move on.

To be blunt: any artist who proudly admits to using AI is being incredibly naive. The companies that actually make the money know how to play the game: leverage AI to the hilt while maintaining a brand image that screams, "We value our artists." They use AI while pretending not to, reap the efficiency, maintain the moral high ground, and deflect any heat with a "trust us" line.

This is the world the anti-AI discourse actually created. It didn't lead to a world without AI. It led to a world where AI is hidden, "laundered," and impossible to pin down.

The "world where corporations kneel before human artists" is a pipe dream. Instead, we’re living in a world where companies lie to cover their tracks, and the only people getting burned are the ones honest enough to admit they use the tools. Anti-AI sentiment didn't stop the tech—it just made the honest people look like fools.

comments.author: Aineisa
comments.body:
Ignore the antis. Do EVERYTHING you can to dev your game with AI before the corps hike the prices. Right now they are giving them out at a loss. Now is the chance. 

And most players won’t care as long as the game looks and plays well so try up your quality and art consistency.
